summary: MSVCRT-style math error handler dispatcher (sub_596175). Reads the error type code at *(DWORD*)a2 and maps type 1 and type 5 to action 8, type 2 to 4, type 3 to 17, type 4 to 18, type 6 to a reset (*(DWORD*)a2 = 1, handler skipped) and type 7 to 16; type 8 falls through with no handler. When sub_5919DA returns nonzero the handler is suppressed; otherwise sub_591727 builds the error-handler argument array. Afterwards the FPU control word is restored and SetErrorCodeBasedOnInputRange(*(DWORD*)a2) is returned when the error type is 8, the FPE exception flag dword_5E9AD0 is set, or StubReturning0() returns NULL.

operations.description: Capture the 16-bit FPU control word at a3 into v3 and read the dispatch key from the error type code at *(DWORD*)a2.

Sequential type dispatch: type 1 and type 5 select action 8; type 2 selects 4; type 3 selects 17; type 4 selects 18; type 6 resets *(DWORD*)a2 to 1 and skips the handler; type 7 selects 16; type 8 falls through without a handler action.
Call sub_5919DA with the selected action, the double operand at (double*)(a2 + 24) and the control word; a nonzero return suppresses the handler setup.
When a1 is 16, 22 or 29, load v15 from (double*)(a2 + 16) and set the low flag bits in the local v16 (v16 & 0xFFFFFFE0 | 3); otherwise clear bit 0 of v16 (v16 &= ~1).
Set up the error-handler argument array via sub_591727((ULONG_PTR)Arguments, &a3, v11, a1, (double*)(a2 + 8), (double*)(a2 + 24)).
Restore the saved FPU control word with ReturnFPUControlWord(v3).
Select the error-code return path when *(DWORD*)a2 equals 8, or when the FPE exception flag dword_5E9AD0[0] is set, or when StubReturning0() returns NULL.
Return SetErrorCodeBasedOnInputRange(*(DWORD*)a2) as the resolved error code.
Invoked from MSVCCRTMathErrorHandler (0x0058DC57) and sub_59070A (0x0059070A) as the CRT math error dispatch entry.

unresolved: Meaning of the action codes 4, 8, 16, 17, 18 and their mapping to MSVCRT _matherr / _fpieee_flt error categories is not evidenced by the packet.
The v16 flag construction (v16 & 0xFFFFFFE0 | 3 / v16 &= ~1) operates on an uninitialized local and is a decompiler artifact; the real caller-visible flag semantics are unknown.
The FPU control word at a3 is a __int16 in the raw source but is passed around as an unsigned 16-bit value; its precise field meanings are not evidenced.
